doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: What the Onyx Club and 52nd Street rooms looked like
summary: The Onyx was a tiny basement room in a brownstone with drinks only, no cover, and five or six sets a night.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: The Onyx packed would have about how many people?
The what?
The Onyx Club, a full house.
I would say if you had 50 people, that place would be running over out into the street – a small joint, a really small joint. It had a bar and a table.
Kitchen? Did they have a kitchen?
No. They didn’t have any food delivery in there.
Did people go and get food and bring it in?
No, they didn’t eat any food in there. It wasn’t a club with any kind of food served in there at all. Just music and drinks. That’s all. They didn’t serve any food.
A waitress? People serving?
Waiters. They had waiters.
I’m just trying to picture it visually. Did – what did it look like?

It’s in the basement of a brownstone. That’s the way 52nd Street was set up. Most of the clubs were in the basement or street level of brownstones in that particular street. There was only one club that I recall – two – one was 21, which is still there, and there was another club that was set up as a comedy club. I can’t remember the name of it. But there was only two standard clubs that weren’t part of an apartment – part of a brownstone or were set up to be a club.
People lived above it?
Yeah. People lived above.
Cover charge?
I don’t think so.
So you pay for the drinks and there would be no . . .?
I don’t recall too much about any kind of cover charge being on in there. You just came in, and they play a set, [?] drinks, and you were served.
9 to 4 would be how many sets?
Roughly you played maybe about 5 – 5 or 6 sets in a night.
The place would be packed?
